Acl.description:
Reusable API schema for access control lists.

Supports two modes (mutually exclusive):

**Replace mode** — send `grants` to replace all entries:

    {"grants": [{"principal_type": "user", "principal": "...", "actions": ["read"]}]}

Use `{"grants": []}` to clear all entries.

**Patch mode** — send `add` and/or `remove`:

    {"add": [...grants...], "remove": [{"principal_type": "user", "principal": "..."}]}

Cannot mix `grants` with `add`/`remove`.

add.description: Patch mode: grants to add or merge into existing

grants.description: Replace mode: full list of grants (replaces all existing). Use [] to clear.

remove.description: Patch mode: principals to remove from existing

AgentCreateResponse.description:
Response shape for `POST /api/v1/agents`. Mirrors `AgentSchema` field-
for-field, plus an optional `installed_configs` array populated only
when the request supplied `template_bundle`.

Field declarations are duplicated rather than imported so the OpenAPI
spec sees a self-contained schema and the API DSL strict cast finds
every field directly on the response object. `from/2` delegates to
`AgentSchema.from/2` for the agent fields and merges the install
configs on top.

acl.description: Access control list. Contains grants array with principal_type, principal, and actions. Null when no ACL restrictions are applied.

installed_configs.description: Present when the request supplied `template_bundle`. One entry per persisted config; `key` echoes the caller-supplied input identifier (original lookup_key for top-level configs; `<skill_lookup_key>:<relative_path>` for skill files). Order is stable: sorted by `key`.

AgentHealthAction.description:
Wire shape for an agent_health_action row, designed for the UI to

the UX needs to build action links — e.g., `key + scope` for env_var
routes the user to the right secret-store form with the field
pre-selected; `installation_kind` for install routes to the right
OAuth flow.

`verify_config` is exposed minus internal resolution details (the
`script_config_id` the install pipeline computed from a bundle-side
`script_ref` is server-side only — UX never invokes the script
directly, the platform does). The retained `verify_config.type`
lets the UX know which kind of "Verify" affordance to render.

PresetConfig.description:
API schema for preset handler configuration.

Mirrors `ArchAstro.Agents.Routines.PresetConfig`. Used wherever a request
or response carries a preset config — routine-level and chain-step-level.

Server-side validation (length/format rules on `instructions`, enum checks
on `session_mode`/`session_scope`, model lookup against
`ChatCompletion.models/0`) is authoritative. This schema defines the
request shape and typed response shape so OpenAPI consumers see real
types instead of an opaque object.

instructions.description: Custom task or behavior instructions for the preset (max 10,000 chars).

llm.description: LLM invocation settings (e.g. a `model` override for this routine/step).

session_mode.description: Session mode: `stateless` (default, new session per trigger) or `session` (find-or-create a persistent session scoped by `session_scope`).

session_scope.description: When `session_mode` is `session`, controls session scoping: `per_user` (default), `per_key`, `per_org`, or `global`.

structured_message_template_ids.description: Config IDs of AgentMessageSchema templates that constrain the agent's responses to predefined structured formats.

RoutinePreset.description:
A routine preset entry in the preset listing endpoint. Describes *what*
a preset is, not a per-routine configuration — that's `PresetConfig`.

applicable_events.description: Event types this preset accepts. `["*"]` means any event. Other event types are rejected at routine validation time.

chainable.description: Whether this preset may appear as a step inside a `:chain` routine. Presets with session or async execution models are not chainable.

sessionable.description: Whether this preset maintains a persistent chatroom session across turns (e.g. `participate`). Sessionable presets don't expose instructions or session-mode fields at the routine level.

unique.description: Whether only one routine with this preset may exist per agent. Enforced at the AgentRoutine unique-index layer.

key.description: Stable category key referenced by Solution.category_keys

owners.description: Owner scopes this category appears under. Members: `"system"` (app-level system scope) and/or `"org"` (viewer's org scope).

name.description: Agent display name. May be null.

SolutionDependentsResponse.description:
Preview for `GET /api/v1/solutions/:solution/dependents`. Reports what
deleting the Solution would do to live agents, without deleting
anything — used to warn in the delete-confirmation UI.

Deleting a Solution never destroys agents: bundled configs that a live
agent still references are kept (detached from the Solution) instead of
deleted. `preserved_config_count` is how many configs that protection
applies to; `dependent_agent_count` is how many agents are affected.

dependent_agent_count.description: Distinct agents with at least one resource referencing a bundled config.

dependent_agents.description: A bounded sample of the dependent agents for display. May be shorter than `dependent_agent_count`.

preserved_config_count.description: Bundled configs that would be kept (orphaned) rather than deleted because a live agent still references them.

SolutionDiffEntry.description: One row in a Solution upgrade response's `changes` array.

SolutionDiffReference.description: External reference to an orphaned config in a Solution upgrade diff.

SolutionDiffSummary.description: Summary counts for a Solution upgrade diff.

SolutionImportResponse.description:
Response shape for `POST /api/v1/solutions` (import). The Solution
config row plus an `installed_configs` array summarising every config
the import transaction persisted alongside it (Solution, skills,
scripts, routine templates, message schemas, etc.).

Pairs with `SolutionInstallResponse` — import puts a Solution into
the library, install provisions a runtime resource (Agent etc.)
from an already-imported Solution.

installed_configs.description: Deprecated legacy field. One entry per persisted config in the import (including the Solution itself), defaulting to an empty array. Callers should prefer `solution` plus follow-up APIs instead. `key` echoes the caller-supplied input identifier (original lookup_key for top-level configs; `<skill_lookup_key>:<relative_path>` for skill / solution-file children). Order is stable: sorted by `key`.

solution.description: Imported Solution in the same shape returned by GET /api/v1/solutions/:solution

SolutionImportResult.description:
Machine-readable result for Solution imports.

Dry-run callers use this to decide whether the import can proceed as
a normal create/update or needs a dedicated upgrade path.

code.description: Conflict code, if status is conflict

dry_run.description: Whether this result came from dry_run

status.description: "ready" when import can proceed; "conflict" when upgrade flow is required

SolutionInstallResponse.description:
Response shape for `POST /api/v1/solutions/:solution/install`.

Install provisions a runtime resource from an already-imported
Solution — the kind of resource depends on what the Solution wraps
(AgentTemplate → Agent, AutomationTemplate → Automation,
AgentRoutineTemplate → AgentRoutine, AgentToolTemplate → AgentTool,
AgentSkillTemplate → AgentSkill, AgentComputerTemplate → AgentComputer).
The response carries that resource's id + kind + lookup_key, plus a
back-pointer to the source Solution.

Pairs with `SolutionImportResponse` — import puts a Solution into
the library; install provisions runtime resources from it.

kind.description: Kind of the provisioned resource: Agent, Automation, AgentRoutine, AgentTool, AgentSkill, or AgentComputer

lookup_key.description: Lookup_key stamped on the provisioned resource (null for AgentSkill, which is a join row with no lookup_key of its own)

solution.description: Source Solution config id (cfg_…) the install was provisioned from

SolutionListResponse.description:
Paginated list response for `GET /api/v1/solutions`. Each entry is a
`SolutionSummary` — see that module for the per-row shape, owner
semantics, and dedupe rules.

SolutionSummary.description:
Catalog row for `GET /api/v1/solutions`. One entry per imported
Solution config — the ID + storage location + vanity fields lifted
from the Solution body, plus the list of owners it appears under
(`"system"`, `"org"`) so callers can tell where it came from.

Multi-owner entries are produced when the same Solution (same
`solution_id`) exists at both the app-level system scope and the
viewer's org scope. The list endpoint dedupes by `solution_id` and
merges the owners list. When the system-scope row's version is
higher than the org-scope row's, `upgrade_available` is `true` and
`latest_version` carries the system version.

category_keys.description: SolutionCategory keys from the Solution body

latest_solution.description: When `upgrade_available` is true, the system-scope Solution config ID that should be used as the upgrade source. Null otherwise.

latest_version.description: When `upgrade_available` is true, the higher system-scope `solution_version` available to upgrade to. Null otherwise.
